aliases: does max 300 apply in the stepladder finals too

aliases: my cut is tied and the tiebreaker can't break it
what happens when a cut is tied
text: If a cut is tied and the configured tiebreaker cannot break it, the desk warns and requires a tournament director decision before you continue.

aliases: how do i add a late bracket entry after brackets are generated
can i add a bracket entry after brackets are generated
text: After brackets are generated, a late entry needs a full Regenerate — you cannot safely patch a single seat into an already generated bracket board.

aliases: who decides a tie in the stepladder finals
text: The tournament director decides stepladder (ladder) ties. There is no automatic pinfall override for an unresolved ladder tie.

aliases: what's the difference between a standard round and a baker round
text: Standard game style scores each bowler's own games. Baker style shares one team score per game (team TOTAL is the sum of team games, max 300 per game). Set game_style on the round's competition method config.

Mystery Doubles is a side-action pot that pairs bowlers by rule after scores are in (partners are not chosen up front). Configure it under Side Actions, take entries, then score and run the pot report.

aliases: what does lock and generate do on a bracket
text: Lock & Generate on a bracket freezes the entry list and builds the bracket board (byes, seats, matchups). After generate, late entries need a full Regenerate.

aliases: what is an eliminator side action
how does eliminator side action work
text: An Eliminator side action is a pot where bowlers drop as the eliminator rules fire (not the same as a main-event eliminator/qualifier round). Configure type Eliminator under Side Actions, take entries, then score.

aliases: what is a survivor side action
text: Victory's side-action types are brackets, high game, eliminator, and related pots (including doubles variants). There is no separate Survivor side-action type — use Eliminator or High Game depending on the pot rules you want.

aliases: what's the difference between scratch and handicap
text: Scratch uses raw pinfall. Handicap adds truncated pins from average so bowlers compete on adjusted scores. Side-action and bracket pots each have their own scratch/handicap setting.
